title: Importing the 'Too-Big-To-Fail' Framework from Finance to AI Ecosystem Risk

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible but with a gap: adapting SIFI criteria to AI is a conceptual exercise that informs policy but does not directly reduce safety risk. Impact depends on regulatory adoption of the framework.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires deep understanding of financial regulation (Basel III SIFI criteria) and AI deployment landscapes. Cross-domain expertise in both finance regulation and AI safety is rare among CS beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The scoring exercise itself is well-scoped: define criteria, score current models. The deliverable is a framework document with model scores. Completable in 30 hours if domain knowledge is available.

novelty.reasoning: The EU AI Act already establishes a systemic risk framework for general-purpose AI models with a concrete threshold (10^25 FLOP for training). Article 55 defines obligations for providers of GPAI models with systemic risk, effective August 2025. The ESRB (December 2025) and FSOC (2024) have both elevated AI as a systemic risk concern. The financial SIFI analogy is implicitly adopted in regulatory frameworks. However, a formal academic mapping of Basel III SIFI criteria specifically to AI models — with scoring methodology and model-by-model assessment — has not been published as a standalone research contribution. The regulatory frameworks partially subsume this idea but from a policy rather than research lens.
